I have come across some inaccuracies and nuanced issues. Worst of all is that BMI is a major factor used to calculate your fitness age. This is a very poor metric to use for individuals with higher muscle-to-fat ratio. I believe it should be a body fat percentage that we can input ourselves. I’m not going to purchase the Garmin Index Scale just so these metrics are accurate.
Sometimes sleep data is off when it comes to times I fell asleep. It doesn’t seem to pick up naps very well, either. Every once in a while, when tracking a workout, the app will ignore the reps or weight I logged on my device (Fenix 9).
I’m looking forward to further use and improvement!

Overall, I really like this app and find it useful for tracking health and wellness.

One adjustment to how it operates that would be most useful to me (personally), would be the ability to freely name/label "exercises" in HIIT workouts. While there are many exercises to choose from in the library, the list is not all-encompassing and the ability to add personal titles to exercises would be more helpful than leaving the exercise labeled as "unknown" or a wholly inaccurate app-generated guess. 

Additionally, (as an NREMT) providing the AHA scale as the only context for blood pressure monitoring is in my opinion poor guidance - as blood pressure is much more nuanced than that scale represents.

reviews.title: Could be so much better
reviews.text:
Garmin Connect provides excellent fitness data, advanced metrics, and workout functionality, but the music/download experience desperately needs improvement.

Managing downloaded playlists and music on a Forerunner 265 is unnecessarily difficult. There should be a simple option in Garmin Connect to view what music is currently downloaded to the watch, add or remove playlists, and force a music refresh directly from the phone. Instead, updating playlists requires navigating through the watch itself and relying on a separate Wi-Fi sync process.

For a smartwatch with otherwise excellent training functionality, this feels outdated and unintuitive. Please make music management part of Garmin Connect and allow users to manage and refresh watch downloads directly from the app.

Some of the problems that I have when it does work when choosing workouts and specific exercise exercises in workouts, it doesn’t allow you to write in the app, the exercise you’re doing and you have to find it from a list of how they have it worded. It makes things a little bit difficult. reviews.title: Superior Data
reviews.text: After having 4 Apple Watches I grew tired of the hamster wheel approach to activity tracking and goals. I was also tired of switching between watches because none of them could last a full day and night for sleep tracking. I purchased an entry level Forerunner and was blown away with how superior both the data and battery were. Intelligent data that was actually useful and only needing a charge once a week? What a dream. The user interface on the app isn’t quite as polished as Apple and has a bit of a learning curve but it’s not that bad; I picked it up quick. There is a lot you can do with building workouts, setting goals, tracking gear and the like. I feel like I use a lot of it but at the same time know I haven’t even scratched the surface really. I thought I would miss smart notifications and some functions more than I do, but I’ve actually enjoyed having a watch that is more watch than a very small not as useful phone on your wrist. Two years in now, absolutely no regrets I’d rebuy this Forerunner 100x over another Apple Watch. I still get nearly 7 days of battery and it works just as good as the first day I wore it. I’ll upgrade eventually but I can tell it won’t be caused by need like all my Apple Watches…it will be my choice. And I’m planning to get a higher end Forerunner that will give me even more useful data — worth every penny!
